visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) An older woman with short dark hair and a black sweater with neon pink and green accents stands on the left. She hands a red envelope to a younger woman sitting on a wooden bench on the right. The younger woman wears a yellow beanie and a yellow hoodie, holding a small brown poodle. In the background is a beige wall with a red festive decoration. (2) The camera moves to a medium shot focusing on the younger woman. She accepts a red envelope while already holding cash in her hand. They exchange smiles and look at each other. The lighting is bright and indoor-based. (3) The scene cuts to a closer perspective of the younger woman alone on the bench with the poodle. She opens the red envelope and pulls out a pair of wooden chopsticks instead of money. Her expression shifts from a smile to utter confusion as she gazes at the chopsticks and then looks towards the off-screen older woman.

narrative_and_purpose.mainPurpose: The video is a humorous skit playing on the Chinese New Year tradition of giving red envelopes (hongbao). The mother tells her daughter to 'take this to eat what you like,' implying the envelope contains money for food. The daughter acts modest but accepts it, only to find the envelope literally contains chopsticks, subverting the expectation of receiving cash and turning the literal meaning of the mother's words into a prank.
